segments.t: Lyova takes Barinov's blood pressure and is shocked by the reading. Then his mother rings, and Lyova has bad news of his own. Here is the scene in Russian first.
Мама, я ни в чём не виноват.
Надо уметь отвечать за свои поступки.
Let's go through this again, a line at a time.
'One hundred sixty over ninety.' 'Sto' is a hundred, 'shestdesyat' is 'six tens', and 'devyanosto' is the odd one, ninety. 'Na' here means 'over', as in a fraction.
'Viktor Petrovich, this is not a joke.' 'Shutki' is the plural of 'joke', and Russians say 'these aren't jokes'. A single 'joke' would be 'shutka'.
'Such pressure is very dangerous.' The dash stands for 'is'. 'Davlenie' comes from 'davit', to press, so blood pressure is a pressing.
'Yes, everything will be fine.' Barinov waves it off with 'will be well'. Russian uses the adverb for 'well' where English says 'fine', and there is no subject.
'Any stress and it will be bad.' 'Lyuboy' means 'any'. The little 'i' means 'and then', so the sentence says 'any stress, and then it will be bad'.
'Hi, Mom.' Lyova uses the full word for mum, not the short form a child would call out. It sounds a little more grown-up.
'How was your workday?' Days 'pass', 'proshyol', in Russian, and 'proshyol' is a man's form because 'den' is masculine. It's the usual way to ask how someone's day went.
'Fine, they fired me.' 'Menya uvolili' is 'me they fired', and nobody is named as the one who did it. 'Normalno' means 'fine'.
'Not fired, but demoted.' 'Ne ... a ...' is the pair for 'not X but Y'. 'Ponizili' means 'lowered', and 'nizky' is 'low', so a demotion is a lowering.
Мама, я ни в чём не виноват.
'Mom, I am not guilty of anything.' 'Ni v chyom ne' is 'in nothing not', with the double negative. 'Vinovat' is 'guilty', in a man's form.
Надо уметь отвечать за свои поступки.
'You must know how to answer for your actions.' 'Umet' is 'to know how', and 'otvechat za' is 'to answer for'. 'Postupki' are deeds, things you do.

'Thank you for the support, Mom.' 'Spasibo tebe' adds 'to you', which makes the thanks personal. 'Za podderzhku' is 'for the support', with the thanked thing after 'za'. Now let's listen to the whole conversation again from start to finish.
Мама, я ни в чём не виноват.
Надо уметь отвечать за свои поступки.
Lyova has been demoted, and his mother has a lecture ready. When you watch, notice what is on the blood pressure monitor. See you next time.

lines.fragment: Не уволили, а понизили в воспитательных целях.
За опоздание. Мама, я не виноват.
Нет-нет-нет. Надо уметь отвечать за свои поступки.
